Pierre Elliott Trudeau was prime minister of Canada from 1968 to 1979 and from 1980 to 1984, the most influential of the late 20th century. A law professor from Montreal, he opposed Quebec separatism.

His government made Canada officially bilingual in 1969 and adopted multiculturalism as policy in 1971. He invoked the War Measures Act in the October Crisis of 1970, and his national energy policy angered the West.

His great achievement was the patriation of the constitution from Britain in 1982 with the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, though Quebec did not sign. He helped defeat the 1980 referendum on Quebec sovereignty that grew from the Quiet Revolution. His son Justin became prime minister in 2015.
sum: Pierre Elliott Trudeau was prime minister of Canada from 1968 to 1979 and from 1980 to 1984, the most influential of the late 20th century. A law professor from Montreal, he opposed Quebec separatism.
